These findings indicate that neomycin could influence Mcl-1 through different molecular mechanisms, potentially by modulating enzyme activity or by acting as a substrate for downstream targets. The scores from the paths suggest a moderate level of confidence in the relationship, with varying degrees of support from different pathways. The evidence highlights the complexity of the interaction network, where neomycin may exert its effects on Mcl-1 through a series of intermediate targets, possibly by altering cellular processes involved in leukemia cell differentiation and survival. The integration of these pathways underscores the importance of considering multiple layers of molecular interaction when evaluating the potential role of neomycin in targeting Mcl-1.
